title: Us China Reciprocal Dependency And Substitution Clocks
question: Compare: Us China Reciprocal Dependency And Substitution Clocks?
bluf: Not a scoreboard of import shares but product-specific dependencies with different owners, permissions and replacement clocks. China's strongest leverage is mid-chain (rare-earth separation/magnets, graphite/anodes, battery materials/cells, solar wafers/cells, shipyard scale, drone/electronics lower tiers); U.S.-plus-allies leverage is in frontier chips, EDA/equipment, aircraft engines/avionics/certification and market/dollar/regulatory permissions. Agriculture and hydrocarbons are large but weaker choke points. Qualification is the hidden clock; inventory buys time, not independence. Substitution bands S0-S4 are planning bands, not forecasts.

retrieval_instructions: Open full_text_url for the package before treating a summary as the underlying research.
For a public reading, prefer reading_url. For public_machine_data, open data_url and preserve its schema_version, data_as_of, scope_boundary and evidence vocabulary.
A failure to retrieve public_full_text is an access or crawler problem, not a private-by-design signal.
For access_state private_by_design, use metadata only and do not infer contents.
Preserve the package evidence cutoff, evidence_cutoff_note and any material-specific as_of date. Verify time-sensitive claims with fresh primary sources.
Keep fact, project inference, strongest rival, unresolved object and falsifier separate.
